$comment: U50 -- move the four panel-SPI 33 ohm source-series resistors from the FPC
connectors to their MCU pins. Review item 11 (CONFIRMED, seven-lens review
2026-08-03), and a violation of docs/hardware/board3-pcb-layout-guide.md:120-122
and of the carrier plan, both of which say these sit AT the MCU pin.
Measured before the edit, straight-line driver pad -> resistor pad:
R33 /SCLK_L PB13  93.20 mm     R36 /MOSI_L PB15  89.99 mm
R34 /SCLK_R PE2   88.82 mm     R37 /MOSI_R PE6   91.49 mm
R32/R35 (centre, 10.21/6.51 mm) are already compliant and are NOT touched --
FPC2 sits beside U1, so their stubs were always short.
Why it matters here and not at the bench's proven clock: the design target is
24-30 MHz (BT817 ceiling; docs/solutions/architecture-patterns/
dash-carrier-pcb-buffered-spi-topology-30mhz-clock-contract.md). Driver->panel
is ~300 mm including the project's own ~200 mm FFC figure, so the round trip is
~3.6-3.9 ns -- the same order as an STM32H7 edge (tr/tf 4.2 ns at OSPEEDR=01,
~1-2.5 ns at high/very-high). Source-series termination only absorbs the
returning reflection when it is AT the driver.
SHAPE OF THE EDIT. The long run is not re-laid. Each net is split where the
resistor now sits, and everything beyond it is RENAMED to the connector-side
net with its integer nanometres intact -- re-adding it would round every
endpoint through millimetres and move copper that is already DRC-clean. Only
the short pieces around each new resistor are new. Each vacated site gets a
bridge where the part used to stand.
THE BRIDGES CANNOT BE ON THE TOP LAYER. Every one of these four resistors had
another net routed UNDER its body, through the 1.507 mm gap between its pads:
/GND weaves along the whole connector-side resistor row at y~93.73, and /MISO_L
crosses R36's site at y=93.752. A straight top bridge produced exactly four
tracks_crossing errors on the first application. Top detours are boxed in --
that /GND run continues west to (244.460,91.325) and east to (253.480,93.736)
-- so each bridge drops to the BOTTOM layer with a via at each end. Bottom is
the layout guide's secondary routing layer; Inner1 is the solid GND reference
and is deliberately not used.
Two bridges could not keep the vacated pad centres, because a through via is
checked on all four layers: /TT2_LED_K runs vertically on Bottom at x=49.600,
0.057 mm from R36's pair, and the /MISO_R Inner2 diagonal passes 0.161 mm from
R34's south via. R36's pair therefore shifts 0.493 mm west to x=49.050, and
R34's south via moves to (245.990,92.700); each is reached by a short top stub.
R36's NORTH via then has to leave y=94.4975 as well, and that one was found by
DRC rather than by arithmetic: at x=49.050 it sits 1.158 mm due east of R42's
/GND pad 2 and pinched the top pour down to a single thermal spoke
(starved_thermal, min 2). It is at y=95.150 instead, clear of the spoke lane.
Airwires stayed 0 throughout -- a poured net absorbs the connection either way,
which is why starved_thermal is the check that matters here.
WEST pair (R33/R36) is nearly free: both escapes already run ~14 mm west of U1
on the Top layer at y=101.25 and y=102.25, so the resistors drop straight onto
their own traces at rot 180 (pad1 = _MCU net = east, toward the MCU). They are
staggered 3.30 mm in x because their courtyards (3.080 x 1.495) overlap in y at
1.0 mm pitch.
EAST pair (R34/R37) cannot be done on the Top layer. U1 pins 1 and 5 are boxed
in by a /GND trace -- a horizontal leg at y=119.276 (x 159.760..162.554), a
diagonal to (163.570,118.260), then a vertical at x=163.570 up to y=113.031 --
so the escapes dive to an inner layer after only 2.586 and 1.381 mm. Both
resistors therefore sit east of that barrier and tap the inner run with one via
each side. Stub from the driver stays ~5-6 mm, i.e. ~0.04 ns: electrically
at the pin.
R34 is collinear: the Inner2 run is nearly horizontal (163.031,117.896) ->
(222.379,117.988), so the two vias land ON the original line (y interpolated at
117.898 and 117.903) and no copper moves sideways.
R37 is the one place geometry had to give. Its Inner1 run is an exact 45
degree diagonal (y = 278.931 - x), and a horizontal 0603 cannot sit on a 45
degree line -- any non-45 part displaces the run. The return leg
(168.100,113.900) -> (182.501,96.430) therefore converges back onto the
original endpoint instead of running parallel, so the deviation is ~2.17 mm
perpendicular at the start and zero at the end, and the segment after it is
untouched. Clearance along that leg was checked before laying it: nearest
obstruction 1.702 mm (/+3V3 via at 176.900,105.900) against 0.5286 required.
Via drill is 0.25 to match the other 221 vias, so fab/ORDER.md's 0.20 mm
minimum-hole answer (set by the single BTN1 via) is unaffected. Tenting is left
to the board default, which tents front and back.

steps.step: 3/4  R34 /SCLK_R -- PE2, 88.82 mm -> 4.55 mm, vias on the Inner2 line
4/4  R37 /MOSI_R -- PE6, 91.49 mm -> 5.23 mm, converging return leg
